0.content:
Akademiya Extravaganza (also: Wisdom Gala, Interdarshan Championship): The Akademiya Extravaganza is the Sumeru Akademiya's festival. It has two parts: the Wisdom Gala, held every year, when the six Darshans set up booths around Sumeru City to attract students, and the Interdarshan Championship, held once every four years, when each Darshan sends one representative to compete for the title of champion, rewards and the right to wear the Diadem of Knowledge. The Championship held in version 3.6 (the event A Parade of Providence) took place after the change in Sumeru's leadership and was of great importance to the Akademiya, which invited many desert-dwellers to enjoy its atmosphere.

Wisdom gala: The Wisdom Gala is held every year. All six Darshans set up booths across Sumeru City to show off what they do and attract potential students. Booths often have minigames and activities.

Interdarshan championship: Held every four years. Each Darshan picks one representative, and they compete to become champion of the entire Championship and earn rewards. For the twenty years up to and including A Parade of Providence, a top prize was the right to wear the Diadem of Knowledge, a valuable treasure widely thought of as a work of art.

Scene use: Use it for bustling Sumeru City scenes: Darshan booths with games, students recruiting, banners, spectators gathered around the Championship's commentators. It is a place where scholars, desert-dwellers and outlanders mingle.

1.content:
Aranara Language (also: Aranara speech, Aranara words, Aranara script): The Aranara language is the community's name for the vocabulary the Aranara, the small forest spirits of Sumeru, weave into their speech. They talk to travellers in ordinary Teyvat speech but use their own words for what matters to them: Nara for humans, Vana for forest, Valuka for desert, Marana for the Withering, and Sarva for the place Aranara and the dead are said to come from and return to. Their words are plant- and forest-flavoured, and many resemble Sanskrit.

Practice: Aranara drop their own words into otherwise plain speech and name outsiders in their own way. They call humans Nara, and typically prefix a human's name with it (for example Nara Varuna).

Regional variation: Aranara speech is bound to the Aranara of Sumeru, found in the forests and, in the dream, in places like Vanarana. Other peoples do not use it, though Sumeru's humans who befriend Aranara learn some words.

Scene use: Let an Aranara speak simply and warmly, then drop in one or two of its own words, explained by context. Do not give long Aranara sentences.

2.content:
Deshret Script (also: Deshret alphabet, Deshret writing, Great Red Sand script): The Deshret Script is the community's name for the writing found on the ruins of the Great Red Sand in Sumeru's desert: on doorways, pillars, obelisks, tombs and Primal Construct inscriptions. It looks like hieroglyphs built from the Teyvat alphabet, and the letters mostly spell out names and words from real-world Egyptian, Persian and Ancient Greek. Sacred Seals and Weathered Obelisks each bear a single character of it.

Practice: It is written without spaces, capitals or punctuation, so fans add these when transcribing. Inscriptions are short: names, titles and single words on doors and monuments.

Regional variation: It belongs to the desert of Sumeru and to the ruins of King Deshret's people. The cities of the rainforest and Sumeru City use a different script, covered under culture.sumeru-script.

Scene use: Use it as colour on a ruin: a door of angular glyphs, a tomb inscription of a few letters. A scholar of the Akademiya might guess at one word.

3.content: Genius Invokation TCG (also: Genius Invokation, Genius Invokation TCG Society, Genius Invokation card game, Casket of Tomes): Genius Invokation TCG is a card-dueling game that is all the rage across Teyvat. Two players each field a team of character cards and spend rolled Elemental Dice on skills and action cards until one side's characters are all defeated. It began in Sumeru, spread through Inazuma's publishing trade, and is now played in taverns and cafes from Mondstadt to Sumeru City, with an official Genius Invokation TCG Society that tracks players and cards.

key: Birthday of the Goddess of Flowers
4.content:
Sabzeruz Festival (also: Sabzeruz, Birthday of the Goddess of Flowers, Dance of Sabzeruz): The Sabzeruz Festival is Sumeru's festival for the birth of Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida), counted as the day the sages found her. It is said to have begun as a birthday party for her predecessor, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, thrown by the Goddess of Flowers, and it became Kusanali's festival after Rukkhadevata died. Its heart is the Dance of Sabzeruz, based on the Goddess of Flowers' own dance. Since Rukkhadevata's death the Akademiya has stopped organising it and treats it as almost non-existent, so it survives through ordinary people, above all around the Grand Bazaar.

Practice: Celebrants hold the Dance of Sabzeruz, set out a Haft-Mewa Feast, hand out Yalda Candies and (in the old days) watch flower carriages parade. Volunteers run the stalls.

Origins: The festival is attributed to the Goddess of Flowers, a friend of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who is said to have first held it for Rukkhadevata's birthday. Its present meaning is the birth of Lesser Lord Kusanali.

Scene use: Use it for Sumeru scenes with stalls, candy boxes, the smell of the Haft-Mewa tables, children lining up for Farris, and a dancer in the Grand Bazaar. It is a good setting for bringing Nahida's followers together.

5.content:
Education in Sumeru (also: Akademiya education, Akademiya academics, Sumeru academic system, Sumeru thesis system): Education in Sumeru means the Sumeru Akademiya, the most prestigious institute of learning in Teyvat and also Sumeru's governing body. Students pass hard entrance exams, join one of the Six Darshans, and advance by passing theses through a review panel. Degrees take a very long time, and many scholars travel the world as Driyosh to gather research. The Matra punish academic misconduct.

Practice: Admission is by entrance exam, and only those who pass are accepted. Study is organised into the Six Darshans, each with a specialty. Students call each other seniors and juniors, and graduation depends on getting a thesis past the review panel.

6.content: Sumeru Cuisine (also: Sumerian cuisine, Sumerian food, Sumeru food, Sumeru cooking): Sumerian cooking is fragrant, spicy and colourful. The rainforest and desert supply many edible flowers, mushrooms, fruits and nuts, and the local saying is that Spice, a seasoning made from dried Harra Fruit, goes well with anything. Flatbread wraps, bean soups, grilled fish and a long list of syrupy, nutty or floral sweets are everyday fare, and coffee is a social drink. Two Sumeru City landmarks define the scene: Lambad's Tavern, the main restaurant, and Puspa Cafe, a long-established coffee shop.

7.content:
Daily Life in Sumeru (also: Sumeru daily life, everyday life in Sumeru, Sumeru customs, life in Sumeru): Everyday life in Sumeru, the Dendro nation of wisdom, is shaped by scholarship. The Sumeru Akademiya is both Teyvat's largest known centre of learning and the body that handles much of the nation's daily government, so people value rationality, practical knowledge and academic achievement. Under the old sages many adults wore Akasha Terminals, took pride in not dreaming, and looked down on the arts; since Chapter III people can dream again and the arts are returning. The land is split between northern rainforest and southern desert, with different peoples, guards and habits in each.

Practice: Common routines: studying, researching and defending theses; consulting the Akasha (formerly) or books; hiring Eremites as bodyguards; trading spices, medicine and goods at Port Ormos and Caravan Ribat; eating fragrant, spicy food with flowers, mushrooms, fruit and nuts; and, in the desert, living by the rules of one's tribe.

8.content:
Sumeru Fashion (also: Sumeru clothing, Sumeru attire, Akademiya uniforms, Eremite attire): Sumeru dress marks people by role more than by region. Akademiya students wear uniforms carrying the Akademiya emblem, and each of the six Darshans has a designated colour. Forest Rangers wear green, with higher-ranking Forest Watchers in lighter green. Eremites wear red scarves; the Corps of Thirty, who guard Sumeru City, wear teal-green ones instead.

Practice: - Akademiya students: men's and women's uniforms bearing the Akademiya emblem. The Sage's attire (worn by Grand Sage Azar) is a separate style.
- Forest Rangers: uniforms for men and women; Forest Watchers wear lighter green than ordinary Rangers.
- Eremites: crimson-red scarves; low-ranking Eremites bear the Eremite Crest (a sun motif over two crossed scimitars in a triangle) on the scarf.
- Corps of Thirty: Eremite-style weapons and uniforms with teal-green scarves marked with a petal-like emblem similar to the Akademiya's.

Scene use: Mention a student's Darshan colour, a ranger's green, a red Eremite scarf or the teal scarf of a Corps of Thirty guard to place a scene quickly in Sumeru.

key: worship of the God of Wisdom
9.content:
Religion in Sumeru (also: Sumeru religion, Sumerian faith, worship of the God of Wisdom, Dendro Archon worship): Sumeru's faith has three strands. In the rainforest people worship the God of Wisdom, the Dendro Archon: first Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who died in the Cataclysm 500 years ago, then her successor Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida). In the desert, many Eremites revere the ancient god-king King Deshret and some hope for his return. The Sumeru Akademiya, which governs the nation, prizes reason and counts "revering gods without acts of devotion" among its sins.

Practice: Worship in Sumeru is mostly small and personal. People tell stories of the old goddess, keep the Sabzeruz Festival and trust the God of Wisdom to protect the land. Eremite devotees of Deshret keep alive dances and customs that descend from ancient worship rituals.

Scene use: Treat Sumeru's faith as mostly affection and story. A character may praise Lesser Lord Kusanali fondly, mention the Sabzeruz Festival, scoff at empty piety like an Akademiya scholar, or speak of King Deshret as an ancestor or a danger depending on their background.

10.content:
Sumeru Script (also: Vedanagari Script, Vedanagari, Sumeru alphabet, Sumeru writing): The Sumeru script is the community's name for the lettering on Sumeru's shop signs, bulletin boards, books and monuments. It resembles Devanagari, with the horizontal line along the top of letters, and is built on the Teyvat alphabet. It mostly writes English, with a number of romanised Arabic, Persian, Sanskrit and Greek texts. Its in-world name is probably Vedanagari, mentioned in Alhaitham's 2024 birthday mail.

Practice: Signs use initials, like most Teyvat scripts: KB for Lambad's Tavern, MK for Menakeri's Treasure Shop, FRG for Sumeru General Goods, DS for the Bimarstan. Writing has no spaces, capitals or punctuation.

Regional variation: It is the script of Sumeru's cities, especially Sumeru City. The desert ruins use a different writing, covered under culture.deshret-script, and the Aranara have their own words.

Scene use: Use it for city colour: signs with a few letters, titles on book spines. A resident reads it without thinking; an outlander guesses.
